faq.q: Does it handle the CGST/SGST vs IGST split automatically?
faq.a: Yes. It compares the supplier state and the place of supply (or customer state): a same-state supply is split into CGST and SGST (half each), while a different-state supply uses IGST. Each line item carries its own GST rate (0/5/12/18/28%), and the tax summary groups totals by rate. GST presets set the whole case — intra-state, inter-state, a specific slab, export/zero-rated, or composition dealer.

faq.q: Can I send the invoice over WhatsApp instead of a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. 'Send on WhatsApp' (and 'Copy as text') produces a plain-text invoice built from the same calculation as the PDF, so the numbers match. There's also 'Export all (ZIP)' which bundles the PDF, a plain-text version, a CSV of line items for your books, and a JSON snapshot you can reload into the tool later.

faq.q: How does invoice numbering and supplier auto-fill work?
faq.a: Invoice numbers auto-increment (INV-0001, INV-0002…) stored under invAutoNum, advancing after each PDF. Your supplier details and bank/UPI info are saved under invSupplierData and restored on your next visit, so you only enter them once. The tool also validates GSTIN format (15 characters) and shows amount-in-words in the Indian system (lakh/crore).

faq.q: Does the PDF show the rupee symbol and Hindi text correctly?
faq.a: Yes, with a caveat. pdf-lib's standard fonts can't encode ₹ or Devanagari, so by default the PDF writes 'Rs.' and drops unsupported characters. When your form actually contains such characters the tool embeds a Unicode font and then draws the real ₹ symbol and Indic text. Three templates (Classic, Modern Blue, Minimal) and an accent colour are available. Confirm GST compliance with your accountant — the tool is a helper.
